text:
Maria K: Quick design review — putting up the chart frame I mocked for the console perf dashboard. Need decisions on a few visualization details before I hand to devs:
- Legend ordering (by series name vs by peak impact)
- Axis label units: `tokens` vs `tokens/s` vs adaptive toggle
- Default smoothing: on with 5-point LOESS or off (opt-in)
- Outlier handling: show raw points, clip to 99th percentile, or fade as 'spike' overlays?
- Accessibility: contrast for lighter series colors and aria labels for legend items

Alex R: I can implement whatever we decide but a couple constraints:
- Our chart lib (ngx-charts wrapper) supports per-series sorting and a unit toggle in the header, but we should avoid >2 toggles in the header.
- Smoothing is cheap client-side (webworker) but hurts point-accurate overlays (debug lines). If we enable smoothing by default, we need a clear toggle.

Sam T: My product take:
- Legend ordering: default to "by impact" (highest median token cost at the selected timespan) — helps surface hotspots.
- Units: prefer an adaptive unit toggle with default = `tokens` and a small unit switcher tooltip: `tokens | tokens/s`.
- Smoothing: opt-out by default. Many customers care about absolute peaks for alerts.

Eva L: Accessibility notes:
- Contrast: light blue series (#8fc1ff) fails AA on white at 12px. Need darker variants or stronger outline.
- Legend items need `aria-pressed` state when toggled off and `aria-label` = "Toggle <series name> visibility".
- Also recommend focus styles for keyboard-only users — 2px solid token color + 3px ring.

Alex R: Dev proposal snippet for the legend toggle behavior (can wire to backend sort key):
```
legendConfig: {
  orderBy: 'impact', // 'name' | 'impact' | 'custom'
  showToggle: true,
  ariaLabelPrefix: 'Toggle series',
}
unitSwitch: {
  default: 'tokens',
  options: ['tokens','tokens/s'],
}
smoothing: {
  enabledByDefault: false,
  algorithm: 'loess',
  window: 5
}
```

Maria K: Love that — short and implementable. A couple copy nits:
- For the unit switch tooltip: "View unit" -> change to "Display unit" (more consistent in console)
- For smoothing toggle label: use "Smooth data (experimental)" and include `?` tooltip explaining it uses a rolling LOESS.

Eva L: Also: when we clip outliers to 99th percentile, we should show a small glyph on the axis at the clip threshold and a tooltip "Values above this line were clipped for visualization" — helps with transparency and avoids hiding real incidents.

Sam T: +1 to glyph. Also put a small affordance to "Show raw spikes" which toggles overlay points for debugging. Default off.

design-bot: Accessibility report linked — https://design-reports.internal/reports/1767501234 — flags: series contrast, missing aria-labels for legend buttons.

Alex R: Plan of action:
- Implement legend ordering by impact (backend sort key) and unit switcher in header — PR target EOW. (owner: @Alex R)
- Add smoothing opt-in only and store per-user preference. (owner: @Alex R)
- Outlier: implement 99th percentile clipping visualization with glyph + "Show raw spikes" overlay. (owner: @Alex R)

Eva L: I'll update colors & write the aria spec and hand to Alex by tomorrow. Also will draft the exact copy for tooltips.

Sam T: I'll update the product doc and confirm that default states (smoothing off, spikes hidden) meet customer expectations.

Maria K: Great — decision summary pinned:
- Legend: order by impact by default, still allow name sort
- Units: adaptive but default `tokens`, small "Display unit" switcher
- Smoothing: disabled by default, opt-in per user, label "Smooth data (experimental)"
- Outliers: clip to 99th pct with glyph + optional "Show raw spikes" overlay
- Accessibility: stronger color choices, aria-labels and keyboard focus styles

Maria K: Assigned owners: Alex R (impl), Eva L (accessibility & copy), Sam T (product doc). Thanks team :rocket:
